intent_en: Rank the groups shown by the share who skip medication because of cost.
narration_support: Americans without insurance are the most likely to skip medication because of the cost. Even Americans with insurance are second.
chart_support: Bar chart comparing the percentage of adults who skipped prescriptions due to cost across several countries, showing the United States (both insured and uninsured) has the highest values relative to the UK, Germany, France, Australia, Switzerland, and Canada.
evidence_note: The narration establishes the ranking of Americans (uninsured first, insured second), while the chart provides the international context showing these rates are significantly higher than in other developed nations.
narrative_goal: Show that uninsured Americans are most likely to skip medication because of cost, while even insured Americans rank second and above every other compared country.
intent_machine: To demonstrate that adults in the United States have significantly higher rates of skipping medication due to cost compared to other developed nations, with uninsured Americans being the most likely to skip prescriptions.
current_model_input: Rank the groups shown by the share who skip medication because of cost.
